Technical Training Guide · v1 · June 2026

How the Sausage Gets Made:
Intelligence, Data & Ask-Anything

A click-by-click guide to how client data flows from raw CSV files all the way to a grounded AI answer. Built for engineers joining the team — no prior context assumed.

01 · Foundations

The Big Picture

AbarVa helps large enterprise IT leaders understand their technology estate, make strategic decisions, and execute sourcing and transformation moves — all grounded in the client's own data, not generic AI guesses.

The golden rule: Every answer AbarVa gives must cite a real source from the client's own data. If the data isn't there, the system says "I don't know" — it does not make something up.

02 · Foundations

The Canonical Tenants

AbarVa is multi-tenant. Every piece of data, every AI answer, and every UI element is scoped to exactly one tenant. A user signed in as Meridian Health can never see First Capital's data — enforced at the database level (Row Level Security) and at the Sentinel reasoning layer (cross-tenant fence).

Note: TENANT_ALIAS_PROFILES in src/lib/tenant/aliases.ts currently registers six profiles: the five V4 demo tenants below plus a legacy northstar entry retained for compatibility. New engineers should treat northstar as a legacy/v1 artifact — it has no V4 data pack and no live retrieval proof.

03 · Foundations

The V4 Data Pack — What's in a Client Dataset?

Every client (tenant) has a synthetic dataset that mimics a real $50B+ enterprise. These live in datasets/{client}-synthetic-v4/. They are NOT real client data — they are high-fidelity synthetic data generated to test the platform at realistic scale.

Synthetic ≠ fake. These datasets are calibrated to be statistically realistic for large enterprises — 180–220 applications, 35–50 initiatives, real vendor names with realistic contract values. The AI treats them as real and reasons about them accordingly.

The 17 File Families (F01–F17 + D19)

Each family is a group of CSV/YAML files. Together they paint a complete picture of the client's IT estate.

04 · Foundations

Database Schema — How Data Lives in Azure Postgres

The database is a private Azure PostgreSQL instance, accessible only through the ACA VNet. All tables are prefixed with enterprise_context_ and are partitioned by tenant_key — so a query for "first-capital" literally cannot touch "meridian-health" rows.

Migration files live at supabase/migrations/ (raw SQL). The key migration is 20260514100000_enterprise_context_layer.sql.

The 9 Core Tables (in data-flow order)

1
enterprise_context_sources
Where did this data come from? One row per data source (e.g., "F12 budget CSV loaded on 2026-06-17"). Columns: tenant_key, source_system, source_key, source_type, display_name, freshness_status, confidence.
Schema exists — row counts vary per tenant; verify per-tenant before claiming live
2
enterprise_context_source_files
One row per uploaded file. Tracks file_hash (dedup), row_count, and links back to the source. Prevents loading the same file twice.
Schema exists — verify per tenant
3
enterprise_context_records
One row per logical entity (one application, one initiative, one vendor contract). Columns: tenant_key, canonical_record_id, record_type, title, source_system, source_sheet, source_row_number, lifecycle_state, payload (JSONB). This is the heart of the schema.
Schema exists — verify per tenant
4
enterprise_context_facts
Individual atomic facts extracted from records. One row per fact: fact_key (e.g. "annual_budget"), fact_type (number/string/date), fact_value (JSONB), fact_text (human-readable), source_row_number. This is what the AI reads to cite specific numbers.
Schema exists — verify per tenant
5
enterprise_context_evidence
Linkage table connecting facts to specific citable locations. Columns: citation_label (e.g. "F12, row 4"), citation_locator (sheet + cell), evidence_pointer, evidence_usable. AI answers MUST cite from this table.
Schema exists — verify per tenant
6
enterprise_context_relationships
Graph edges between records. E.g. "FIS Core Banking (app) → Retail Deposits (business function)". Enables AI to reason about connections. ~1,050 edges per client from the graph/ folder.
Schema exists — verify per tenant
7
enterprise_context_chunks
Text chunks for full-text and vector search. Each record is split into ~500-token chunks. Columns: chunk_text, token_count, embedding_status (pending/done), embedded_at. This is what the search query hits.
Partial
8
data_inventory_segments
Coverage score per data segment (org_structure, it_landscape, it_financials, vendor_contracts, etc.). The Context Explorer reads from here to show "8 of 16 dimensions loaded." Columns: segment_name, coverage_score, health_state, record_count.
Schema exists — verify per tenant
9
knowledge_sources
Industry/corpus knowledge NOT specific to any client — analyst reports, benchmarks, best-practice frameworks. Columns: title, publisher, content_type, industry_tags, topic_tags. Provides market context for AI answers.
Partial

Real Example — What a Fact Row Looks Like

When the AI answers "What is First Capital's FY26 IT budget?", it reads from enterprise_context_facts:

tenant_key    | first-capital
record_id     | FCF-BUDGET-FY26-TOTAL

fact_value    | {"amount": 342000000, "currency": "USD", "fiscal_year": "FY26"}
fact_text     | $342M total FY26 IT budget

-- enterprise_context_evidence (citation)

citation_locator | Sheet: Financials, Row: 1, Col: budget_total

05 · Ingestion

Loading a New Client — Step by Step

This is the full process to onboard a brand-new client tenant from scratch, starting with raw data files all the way to a live, queryable client in the app.

Do not claim "loaded" until all 10 states are verified. "Local artifact generated" and "context committed to DB" are two different things. Each state must be confirmed separately.
  • 1
    Create the V4 dataset folder Create datasets/{new-client}-synthetic-v4/ with the 17 file families. Either generate synthetic CSVs or supply real client data in the same schema. 📁 datasets/northstar-clinical-tech-synthetic-v4/
  • 2
    Write manifest.yaml Define tenant_key, client_id (new UUID), display_name, industry, and all load_entries in the correct dependency order (F01 before F05, F05 before F12, etc.). 📄 datasets/{client}-synthetic-v4/manifest.yaml
  • 3
    Insert client row in the DB Run the seed script or admin mutation to INSERT a row into the clients table with tenant_key, slug, name, and industry. This is what resolveTenant() queries when routing users. 📄 src/scripts/seed-client.ts (or via Admin UI)
  • 4
    Add tenant alias Add an entry to TENANT_ALIAS_PROFILES so the app knows how to map the Clerk session's client key to the canonical tenant key. Without this, the app resolves to "unknown" tenant. 📄 src/lib/tenant/aliases.ts
  • 5
    Run the Admin bulk loader Run the substrate loader script directly — npm run load:enterprise-context is not a package.json script. Use the governed operator path: npx tsx src/scripts/seed/load-tenant-substrate.ts --tenant=first-capital (or the tenant-specific seed script if one exists, e.g. npm run seed:skyharbor). This reads the manifest, parses each CSV/YAML, and upserts rows into enterprise_context_sources → records → facts → evidence → chunks. Allow 3–15 minutes for a full V4 pack. Always run inside the private VNet via an ACA job — direct localhost calls cannot reach the Azure PostgreSQL private endpoint. 📄 src/scripts/seed/load-tenant-substrate.ts · src/scripts/embed-pending-chunks.ts
  • 6
    Embed pending chunks The loader creates chunks with embedding_status = 'pending'. Run the embedding job to generate vector embeddings via the OpenAI or Anthropic embedding API. Required for semantic search. 📄 src/scripts/embed-pending-chunks.ts
  • 7
    Build Tower v4 data script Verify that buildTowerV2V4DataScript({clientKey: 'new-client'}) resolves the correct dataset folder and can parse F12 + F11 + T01 + T07 without errors. Check the Tower iframe renders with real program data. 📄 src/lib/tower-v2/v4-data.ts
  • 8
    Run golden questions Execute the 3–5 golden questions from 99-verification/golden-questions.json against the live signed-in session. Every question must return a cited answer with no hallucination. This is proof the pipeline works end-to-end. 📄 datasets/{client}-synthetic-v4/99-verification/golden-questions.json
  • 9
    Create Clerk user(s) Create test user accounts in Clerk (or invite real client contacts). Map their email domain or metadata to the new tenant_key. Without this step, no one can sign in as the new client. 🔑 Clerk Dashboard → Users → Invite
  • 10
    Verify signed-in retrieval Sign in as the new client user. Ask a question in Intelligence. Confirm the answer references real data from the dataset. Confirm no cross-tenant data leaks (ask about another client's data — should return "I don't have information on that"). 🌐 app.abarva.ai/intelligence

Path B: Manifest-Driven Bulk Reload

Used when adding an entirely new file family or re-loading after data corrections. Update the manifest, then re-run the loader. Rows are upserted (not duplicated) because each record has a canonical_record_id derived from the file + row. Existing rows are updated, new rows are added.

07 · Ingestion

How Changes Propagate to Each Layer

What changedIntelligence "Ask"Tower DashboardContext Explorer countsTime to live
New CSV uploaded via Admin Auto Next query picks up new facts (Postgres full-text is live) Manual Tower reads CSV files at page load — must update datasets/ folder AND redeploy Auto Segment coverage score recalculates on next load Intelligence: seconds · Tower: next deploy
New embedding generated Auto Vector search now includes new chunk N/A Tower doesn't use vector search N/A Seconds after embed job completes
V4 CSV file updated on disk Not auto Must re-run loader to push to DB Not auto Tower reads CSV files baked into the image at build time via buildTowerV2V4DataScript. A file change on disk is NOT live until it is committed, the Docker image is rebuilt, and the ACA revision is deployed. Not auto Re-run loader Both: after commit → image build → ACA deploy (~5–10 min)
New Sentinel reasoning logic Auto Next code deploy activates new logic N/A N/A ACA redeploy ~3-5 minutes
Intelligence binding payload (all-tenants.json) Manual Must regenerate + commit file to branch N/A Drives The payload IS the Context Explorer's signal/context/corpus data Manual regeneration step — this is a known gap
The Intelligence binding payload is currently static. The outputs/intelligence-binding/all-tenants.json file is committed to the branch and not auto-regenerated when context data changes. This means the Intelligence v2 surface's signal cards and trust line numbers can go stale if the DB is updated. Automating payload regeneration is a known gap.
08 · Intelligence Flows

How "Ask" Works — The Full Intelligence Pipeline

When a user types a question in the Intelligence ask bar and hits Enter, here is every step that happens — including which file handles it and what the Postgres query looks like.

Real example: Anand, signed in as Meridian Health, types: "Which of our vendors has the highest renewal risk?"
  • 1
    Browser → API: POST /api/intelligence/ask?q=which+of+our+vendors... The IntelligenceV2Surface component calls fetch('/api/intelligence/ask?q=...'). The Clerk session cookie travels with the request automatically — no manual token handling needed. 📄 src/components/intelligence-v2/IntelligenceV2Surface.tsx
  • 2
    Auth: Who is this user? currentUser() from Clerk validates the session and returns the Clerk user object. If no valid session → 401 Unauthorized. The user ID and email are used to look up the person record. 📄 src/app/api/intelligence/ask/route.ts · handleAsk()
  • 3
    Tenant resolution: Which client's data do we use? resolveTenant() runs the resolution chain (URL → cookie → session → email). For Anand at Meridian, this returns tenant_key = 'meridian-health'. All subsequent DB queries are scoped to this tenant_key. 📄 src/lib/tenant/resolveTenant.ts
  • 4
    Session memory: What has this user asked before? prepareAskSessionMemory() loads the last N turns of conversation for this user+tenant. This lets Sentinel understand "who is DXC?" when the user's previous question was about DXC's contract. 📄 src/lib/intelligence/ask/session-memory.ts
  • 5
    Intent classification: What kind of question is this? classifySentinelIntent() keyword-scores the query against IT_PRODUCTIVITY_TERMS and calls Claude for classification. "Vendor renewal risk" → classified as vendor_contracts intent. This routes to the right retrieval strategy. 📄 src/lib/agents/sentinel-reasoning/intent-classifier.ts
  • 6
    Context retrieval: Pull relevant facts from the database Multiple retrieval methods run in parallel:
    • Full-text: SELECT * FROM enterprise_context_chunks WHERE tenant_key='meridian-health' AND (chunk_text ILIKE '%vendor%' OR chunk_text ILIKE '%renewal%')
    • Structured: SELECT * FROM enterprise_context_facts WHERE tenant_key='meridian-health' AND fact_key LIKE '%vendor%'
    • Vector search: semantic similarity on embeddings     📄 src/lib/intelligence/ask/index.ts · retrieveTenantEnterpriseSources()
  • 7
    Context assembly: Build the Claude prompt assembleUserContextBlock() takes retrieved facts + user session context and formats them into a structured prompt block. Each fact includes its citation label ("F11, row 14"). This becomes the grounding context for Claude. 📄 src/lib/agent/prompts/_shared/user-context.ts
  • 8
    Sentinel reasoning: Claude synthesizes an answer runSentinelReasoning() calls Claude with the assembled context. Claude is instructed: "Only state facts that are in the provided context. Every claim must include its citation. If you cannot answer from the context, say 'I don't have sufficient information.'" The response streams back token by token. 📄 src/lib/agents/sentinel-reasoning/index.ts
  • 9
    Claim validation: Strip uncited statements validateClaimsAndCitations() parses Claude's response. Any sentence that makes a factual claim without a citation label gets removed before the response is sent to the user. This is the anti-hallucination gate. 📄 src/lib/agent-claims.ts
  • 10
    Stream to UI + save turn The validated response streams to the browser. In parallel, appendAskSessionTurn() saves this Q&A pair to session memory so future questions can reference it. Telemetry is logged via recordSynthesisEvent(). 📄 src/lib/intelligence/ask/session-memory.ts · src/lib/reasoning/synthesis-telemetry.ts
Result for Meridian: "Your highest renewal risk vendor is DXC Technology (F11, row 8), with a $14.2M/year contract renewing in September 2026 — 3 months away. No renewal owner is currently assigned. The second-highest is Epic Systems (F11, row 2), $22.4M/year, renewing Q2 FY27."
09 · Intelligence Flows

Tower Data Flow — How the IT Dashboard Works

Tower is architecturally different from Intelligence. It uses a self-contained iframe that loads a static HTML/JS application, pre-injected with the client's data. There is no AI call for Tower's ask bar today — answers come from client-side JavaScript pattern matching.

Tower is data-smart but not AI-smart. It knows the numbers because it reads the same CSVs the loader uses. But its "ask" answers are hardcoded regex patterns, not Sentinel reasoning. This is a known architectural gap.

When a User Navigates to /tower

  • 1
    TowerPage (Server Component) runs getActiveClientRow() resolves the tenant. For Meridian: clientKey = 'meridian'. The iframe src is set to /api/tower/v2-frame?client=meridian. 📄 src/app/(maestro)/tower/page.tsx
  • 2
    GET /api/tower/v2-frame?client=meridian runs server-side buildTowerV2V4DataScript({clientKey: 'meridian'}) is called. It looks up the dataset folder: datasets/meridian-health-synthetic-v4/ and reads 6 CSV files from disk. 📄 src/app/api/tower/v2-frame/route.ts · src/lib/tower-v2/v4-data.ts
  • 3
    CSVs → JavaScript data script The 6 CSV files are parsed and converted into JavaScript constants that look like this (injected into the HTML at page load): window.PROGRAMS = [{id:"P001", name:"Epic and Clinical Systems", budget:174800000, ytd:94400000, ...}]; window.VENDORS = [{name:"Epic Systems", acv:22400000, renew:"Q2 FY27", months:9}]; The 6 CSVs: F12 (budget) · F11 (vendors) · T01 (initiative registry) · T07 (benefit realization) · T08 (spend) · T12 (actions)
  • 4
    HTML template → served as iframe The static public/tower-v2/index.html template is injected with: the tenant name, the JavaScript data script, and the AbarVa logo. The inner topbar is hidden via EMBED_CSS (.topbar { display:none }). The full HTML is returned as the iframe's document. 📄 public/tower-v2/index.html · public/tower-v2/app.js
  • 5
    User asks: "How much do we spend on Epic?" answerFor("How much do we spend on Epic?") runs entirely in the browser. It splits "Epic and Clinical Systems" into words ["epic", "and", "clinical", "systems"], filters to words longer than 3 chars, finds "epic" matches the query, and returns the program's budget/YTD data directly from window.PROGRAMS. 📄 public/tower-v2/app.js · answerFor() · programMatch lookup
  • 6
    Bar chart renders — no network call made The answer renders with a bar chart: Budget ($174.8M) vs YTD Spent ($94.4M). The chart is drawn using inline SVG, all client-side. Zero AI, zero API calls — everything came from the injected CSV data. 📄 public/tower-v2/app.js · ansBarChart()
10 · Intelligence Flows

Context Retrieval — How a Question Becomes a Database Query

The AgentContextBroker is the gatekeeper between AI agents and the database. No AI agent directly queries Postgres — everything goes through the broker, which enforces tenant isolation and retrieval strategy.

The Broker Decision Tree

Step 1
Has this tenant been loaded to the private DB?
TenantDataAdapter.hasPersistedData(tenantKey)
↓ Yes                                 ↓ No
Live DB retrieval
buildEnterpriseAgentContextBundleAsync()
Fixture fallback
EnterpriseDataRoom static data

Live DB Retrieval — The 7 Segments Fetched

SegmentPostgres query (simplified)What it returns for "vendor renewal risk"
org_structure SELECT * FROM enterprise_context_records WHERE tenant_key='meridian-health' AND record_type='org_unit' Business unit names, IT owners — gives context for "who owns vendor decisions"
vendor_contracts SELECT * FROM enterprise_context_facts WHERE tenant_key='meridian-health' AND (fact_key LIKE '%vendor%' OR fact_key LIKE '%contract%') All vendor names, ACVs, renewal dates — the direct answer source
it_financials SELECT * FROM enterprise_context_facts WHERE tenant_key='meridian-health' AND (fact_key LIKE '%budget%' OR fact_key LIKE '%spend%') Budget context — how much spend is at risk from unrenewed contracts
program_inventory SELECT * FROM data_segment_program_inventory WHERE tenant_key='meridian-health' Programs that depend on at-risk vendors
evidence_ledger SELECT * FROM enterprise_context_evidence WHERE tenant_key='meridian-health' AND evidence_usable=true Citable sources for every fact (required for anti-hallucination)
kpi_dictionary SELECT * FROM data_segment_kpi_dictionary WHERE tenant_key='meridian-health' Outcome KPIs linked to vendor relationships
cross_program_signals SELECT * FROM data_segment_cross_program_signals WHERE tenant_key='meridian-health' Signals linking vendor risk to program delivery risk

Full-Text Chunk Search

-- Searches the text chunks for keywords from the user's query
SELECT chunk_id, chunk_text, source_record_id, provenance
FROM enterprise_context_chunks
WHERE tenant_key = 'meridian-health'
  AND chunk_text ILIKE '%vendor%'
  AND chunk_text ILIKE '%renewal%'
  AND lifecycle_state = 'active'
LIMIT 20;

Gaps — What Exists vs What's Needed

This is the honest current-state audit of all three "Ask" surfaces against the three layers required for smart, non-hallucinating, rich-output answers.

Surface Layer 1: Substrate
Data the AI can read from		 Layer 2: Grounding
Anti-hallucination contract		 Layer 3: Output Schema
Tables, charts, citations		 Overall
Intelligence
Sentinel / ask bar		 Partial Schema exists and full-text search is live. Embedding status varies per tenant (verify COUNT WHERE embedding_status='embedded'). Semantic/vector retrieval is dormant until pgvector migration (ADR-001) completes. Claims of "done" require signed-in retrieval proof per tenant. Done Sentinel governed contract, citation gate, refuse-on-insufficient, cross-tenant fence Missing Returns plain streaming text only. No structured JSON schema. No table or chart renderer. 70%
Home
Context Explorer ask		 Done Same substrate as Intelligence — data is there Partial Needs to be wired to /api/intelligence/ask (not yet done) Missing Same gap as Intelligence 50%
Tower
Atlas ask bar		 Client-side only V4 CSV data injected at page load into browser JS. Server-side Sentinel cannot read it. Data-bound No hallucination because it's pattern matching, not AI. But not "smart" — can't reason across data. Local only ansBarChart() / stackBar() work in browser but are hardcoded responses, not AI-generated charts. 40%

Build Order for Full Smart Ask

  • 1
    Intelligence: Add structured output schema Modify the Sentinel prompt to return structured JSON: { prose, table?: {headers, rows}, chart?: {type, labels, series}, citations[] } via Claude tool call. Add a table/chart renderer to IntelligenceV2Surface. Estimated effort: 1–2 days.
  • 2
    Home: Wire to /api/intelligence/ask Same pattern as Intelligence v2. The Context Explorer ask bar should call the same route. Share the renderer component. Estimated effort: 0.5 days.
  • 3
    Tower: Commit v4 data to context layer The Tower v4 CSVs (F12, F11, T01, T07) are already loaded into enterprise_context_* for clients where the loader has run. Tower's ask bar should POST to /api/intelligence/ask (not do client-side pattern matching). The Sentinel pipeline will retrieve the same program/vendor data from Postgres. The bar chart renderer becomes the output schema's chart component. Estimated effort: 2–3 days.
  • 4
    Automate binding payload regeneration The outputs/intelligence-binding/all-tenants.json that powers Intelligence v2's signal cards is currently static. Wire a nightly job (ACA scheduled job or GitHub Actions cron) that re-runs getDerivedEnterpriseReadForTenant() for all active tenants and commits the updated payload. Estimated effort: 1 day.
Key principle for new engineers: The anti-hallucination contract is not a prompt trick — it's an architectural constraint. The AI can only cite from enterprise_context_evidence rows where evidence_usable = true. If the data isn't loaded to that table, the answer is "I don't have sufficient information" — never a guess.
